svg.text: The piece runs as one long chain from an old, fixed-wiring model of the brain down to a theory of consciousness,
with a single hub in the middle — Spatial Computing theory — that branches sideways into two explanatory asides

g.text: From fixed neurons to wave-based consciousness
A top-to-bottom chain of argument, with the central mechanism (alpha/beta 'stencils') branching into two explanatory
asides before the chain continues on to consciousness and its rivals.

g.title: One neuron, one fixed job — old connectionist view — The classical model: hierarchical feedforward circuits where each neuron has a stable, specialized meaning. — → spya-k046f6
Most neurons do many jobs at once — mixed selectivity — Cortical neurons blend sensory, motor, and contextual signals rather than having one fixed function. — → spya-v0gbwq
g.text: Most neurons do many jobs at once

g.title: Waves route neuron firing — oscillations organize info — Brain waves segregate spiking by phase and open timing windows for communication between regions. — → spya-jnp59d
Waves nudge neurons directly — ephaptic coupling, no synapse — Electric fields from spiking activity directly shift nearby neurons' voltage, bypassing synapses entirely. — → spya-mapqhv

Alpha/beta gates where gamma fires — Spatial Computing theory — Spatially patterned alpha/beta rhythms act as inhibitory 'stencils' that suppress gamma and spiking in targeted locations. — → spya-qck2sw
Explains mixed selectivity — same neuron, different context — A neuron can fall inside the suppressive stencil in one context and outside it in another. — → spya-zmknun
Explains subspace coding — population stays low-dimensional — Alpha/beta control sorts spiking into structured, overlapping active subsets — orthogonal subspaces. — → spya-m63zb9
Traveling waves shift the active code — moving stencils change what fires — Alpha/beta traveling waves may move population activity from one coding subspace to another. — → spya-y09vju
Wave interference computes directly — analog computing, efficient — Overlapping waves add and cancel according to physics, performing computation in parallel at low energy cost. — → spya-h5qjz4
All anesthetics cause slow, scrambled waves — loss of consciousness — Despite different molecular targets, anesthetics converge on the same disorganized wave pattern. — → spya-uvev07
Synapses store; waves select & bind — hybrid framework — Synapses hold long-term knowledge; brain waves determine which parts of it are active moment to moment. — → spya-dnv2tp

Compared to Global Workspace, IIT, Higher-Order theories — waves, not broadcast or hot-zone — The framework shares themes with rival theories of consciousness but locates the mechanism in wave dynamics. — → spya-xn7mdj
Cognition = organized wave dynamics — conclusion — Brain-wide wave organization, not discrete circuit exchange, is proposed as the basis of cognition and consciousness. — → spya-smkrcs

g.text: A hub-and-aside diagram: the single mechanism of alpha/beta 'stencils' is backed by three pieces of evidence and,
separately, solves two distinct puzzles about neural coding.

g.title: Alpha/beta forms inhibitory 'stencils' — suppresses gamma in some spots — Spatially patterned alpha/beta rhythms act as temporary inhibitory templates across the cortical surface. — → spya-hcav4k
Less beta = more spiking, more movement — In motor cortex, beta acts as a brake; when it drops locally, gamma and spiking rise and movement follows. — → spya-thnz7b
Confirmed in primate prefrontal recordings — context patterns predict errors — Alpha/beta spatial patterns tracked learned context and mismatches predicted behavioral mistakes. — → spya-azz3c8
Alpha/beta's reach fits top-down control — finer than theta, coarser than gamma — Wave spatial scale grows with lower frequency; alpha/beta sits at a few millimeters, apt for control. — → spya-q606tk
g.text: finer than theta, coarser than gamma

g.title: Same neuron differs by context — nonlinear mixed selectivity — A neuron can lie inside the suppressive stencil in one context and outside it in another. — → spya-zmknun
Population activity stays low-dimensional — orthogonal subspace coding — Alpha/beta control sorts spiking into structured, partially overlapping subsets with distinct correlations. — → spya-m63zb9
No fixed 'context neurons' needed — Mixed selectivity arises from interaction, not from specialized neurons with fixed tuning. — → spya-ee45vr
Reconciles noisy cells, ordered populations — Single neurons look noisy and context-dependent, yet populations move together in structured, low-dimensional trajectories. — → spya-qsz9ur

g.text: A chain of evidence (anesthesia, then the hybrid framework) that ends by fanning out into three separate comparisons

g.title: Different drugs, same cortical effect — propofol, ketamine, dexmedetomidine — Despite acting on different molecular targets, these anesthetics converge on the same large-scale electrical effect. — → spya-wnqgmn

All produce slow, scrambled waves — needs organized waves, not a specific drug — Consciousness seems to depend less on specific receptors and more on the integrity of large-scale wave organization. — → spya-k02vdw
g.text: needs organized waves, not a specific drug

g.title: Synapses store; waves pick what's active — Synaptic connections store long-term information; brain waves determine which representations are active now. — → spya-f0dqyd
Waves bind scattered activity into one state — Brain waves dynamically link distributed neural representations into a unified conscious experience. — → spya-tdqde5
Unlike Global Workspace/IIT: fields, not broadcast or hot-zone — Integration happens through dynamic field interactions, not broadcasting of information or a fixed 'hot zone'. — → spya-m3dn2u

Unlike Higher-Order theories: organizing is the consciousness — Rather than a separate system making a state conscious, the act of top-down wave organization is itself the conscious integration. — → spya-nkg5v2
Unlike executive-control models: waves, not synaptic gating — Top-down control is grounded in wave dynamics rather than excitatory synaptic gating of winner-take-all circuits. — → spya-j6qfz4
